Random draws, in R

Source: R/rng.R
zl_rng_uniform.Rd

zl_rng_uniform() and zl_rng_normal() return the single-precision values that zl_noise_uniform() and zl_noise_normal() give inside a graph for the same stream, step and positions: positions offset to offset + prod(dim) - 1 of the stream named stream at step step. Uniforms lie strictly inside (0, 1); normals have mean 0 and standard deviation 1.

Usage

zl_rng_uniform(dim, stream, step = 0, offset = 0)

zl_rng_normal(dim, stream, step = 0, offset = 0)

Arguments

dim

Dimensions: one to four positive whole numbers.

stream

The stream's name.

step

The step number (a trainer's step count; 0 for none).

offset

The position of the first value.

Value

A double vector or array of dimensions dim.

Details

The values are 'zurand”s, rounded to single precision: a uniform is rounded towards zero (so it never becomes 1), a normal to nearest. With the session key k, a uniform equals zurand::rng_uniform( zurand::rng_fold(zurand::rng_fold(k, stream), step), n, offset = offset) so rounded.

Examples

zl_seed(1)
zl_rng_uniform(c(2, 3), "noise")
#>           [,1]      [,2]       [,3]
#> [1,] 0.4639272 0.4965113 0.04710322
#> [2,] 0.4593310 0.3300929 0.53220999
zl_rng_normal(4, "noise", step = 2)
#> [1]  1.8157096 -1.6734138 -1.5309385  0.7882175
